title: Teacher Dashboard — State Assessment Programme
notes:
Discovery workshop — Teacher dashboard for state assessment programme — 18 Feb 2026

Anita Deshmukh (Programme Director, State Education Dept): We're rolling this out to about 12,000 government primary school teachers across the state. Teachers need a dashboard where they can see their own class's foundational literacy and numeracy scores after each assessment cycle, in the language they teach in.

Rohan Bhatt (Master Trainer): A lot of these teachers have only basic smartphones and unreliable data connectivity, especially in the tribal blocks. The dashboard has to load in under 5 seconds on a 3G connection, or teachers just won't use it — we saw that with the last app we rolled out.

Kavita Suresh (Field Coordinator): Assessment data currently comes from bubble sheets that get scanned at the block level. The dashboard needs to pull scanned assessment results from the existing OMR scanning system once they're processed — we're not changing how the scanning happens.

Anita Deshmukh (Programme Director, State Education Dept): Teachers should be able to see which specific learning outcomes their students are struggling with — not just an overall score, but a breakdown by competency, like "cannot read a simple paragraph" versus "reading fluently."

Rohan Bhatt (Master Trainer): Ideally the dashboard would also suggest a remedial activity for each weak competency, pulled from the existing worksheet library, so teachers don't have to search for material themselves.

Kavita Suresh (Field Coordinator): Block education officers need a rollup view — average scores across all schools in their block, so they can see which schools need support without visiting each one individually.

Anita Deshmukh (Programme Director, State Education Dept): This has to work in three languages at minimum for this phase — Hindi, Marathi, and English. Other regional languages would be nice for later but that's not this year's scope.

Imran Sheikh (Tech Lead, Implementation Partner): For data volume — we're expecting about 3.5 million individual student assessment records per cycle, four cycles a year. The dashboard queries need to stay responsive even as that history builds up over multiple years.

Kavita Suresh (Field Coordinator): One thing that's out of scope — this dashboard is read-only for teachers. We are not building any feature for teachers to edit or override assessment scores; corrections go through the block office process that already exists.

Rohan Bhatt (Master Trainer): Data privacy is a real concern — individual student scores should only be visible to that student's own teacher and their block officer, not to other teachers in the school.

Anita Deshmukh (Programme Director, State Education Dept): I remember our pilot last year where a teacher accidentally saw another section's data and it became a whole issue with parents, so that access control really matters to us.

Imran Sheikh (Tech Lead, Implementation Partner): We need at least three years of historical assessment data retained so the department can track cohort progress over a child's schooling.

Anita Deshmukh (Programme Director, State Education Dept): Budget for this phase is fixed at 60 lakh rupees, already approved, and it has to be ready before the next assessment cycle starts in June — that date isn't moving, it's tied to the academic calendar.
